contentRules.title: Reverse shell
contentRules.description: Code that gives a remote attacker a shell on your machine.

contentRules.title: Discord token stealer signature
contentRules.description: Regex or file paths used by Discord token grabbers.

contentRules.title: Browser password/cookie theft
contentRules.description: Reads saved browser passwords, cookies or the Chrome master key.

contentRules.title: Disables antivirus
contentRules.description: Turns off Windows Defender or adds exclusions so malware isn't detected.

contentRules.title: Adds antivirus exclusions
contentRules.description: Adds Windows Defender exclusions so files/processes aren't scanned. Some legit tools do this for speed, but malware does it to hide.

contentRules.title: Crypto wallet theft
contentRules.description: Targets crypto wallet files or wallet browser extensions.

contentRules.title: Crypto miner
contentRules.description: References to cryptocurrency mining software or pools.

contentRules.title: PowerShell download-and-run
contentRules.description: Downloads code from the internet and executes it immediately.

contentRules.title: Encoded PowerShell command
contentRules.description: Hidden PowerShell command passed as base64.

contentRules.title: Executes hidden/encoded code
contentRules.description: Decodes an obfuscated blob (base64/hex/zlib/marshal) and executes it.

contentRules.title: Discord webhook (data exfiltration)
contentRules.description: Hardcoded Discord webhook - a common way stealers send your data to the attacker.

contentRules.title: Install script downloads and runs code
contentRules.description: Package install/setup step fetches remote code and pipes it into a shell or interpreter.

contentRules.title: Downloads and runs remote script
contentRules.description: Pipes a downloaded script straight into a shell (curl | bash).

contentRules.title: Hardcoded Telegram bot token
contentRules.description: Telegram bot API with embedded token - used legitimately by bots but also by stealers to exfiltrate data.

contentRules.title: Startup persistence
contentRules.description: Makes a program start automatically (Run keys, scheduled tasks, cron, LaunchAgents).

contentRules.title: Obfuscated JavaScript
contentRules.description: Heavily obfuscated JS (javascript-obfuscator style _0x identifiers) hides what the code does.

contentRules.title: Obfuscated Python
contentRules.description: Uses a Python obfuscator/packer often seen in malware.

contentRules.title: Large hex-escaped blob
contentRules.description: Long run of \x escape bytes - typical of embedded shellcode or hidden payloads.

contentRules.title: Hidden bidirectional Unicode
contentRules.description: Invisible bidi control characters can make code look different from what runs (Trojan Source).

contentRules.title: setup.py runs commands / network
contentRules.description: setup.py executes commands or makes network requests at install time.

contentRules.title: Fetches from paste/file-drop site
contentRules.description: Pulls content from pastebins, file-drop or tunnel hosts often used to stage malware.

contentRules.title: Downloads an executable
contentRules.description: Hardcoded URL to an executable/script file.

contentRules.title: npm install hook
contentRules.description: package.json runs a script automatically when installed. Usually harmless (build steps) but a common malware entry point.

contentRules.title: URL with raw IP address
contentRules.description: Connects to a hardcoded IP instead of a domain name.

contentRules.title: Large base64 blob
contentRules.description: Very long base64 string embedded in code (can hide payloads; also used for legit assets).

contentRules.title: README tells you to disable antivirus
contentRules.description: Legit software almost never asks you to turn off your antivirus - a classic malware lure.

contentRules.title: Password-protected download
contentRules.description: Password-protected archives are used to sneak malware past scanners.

contentRules.title: README asks to run as administrator
contentRules.description: Asks you to run the program with admin rights.

contentRules.title: README tells you to paste a download-and-run command
contentRules.description: Asks you to paste a PowerShell/mshta command that downloads and executes code from the internet - a very common malware trick ("ClickFix").

contentRules.title: README install pipes a download into a shell
contentRules.description: Install instructions use curl/wget | bash. Common for legit tools, but you run whatever the server sends - only do it for projects you trust.

contentRules.title: Download hosted outside GitHub
contentRules.description: README sends you to a file-sharing site (MediaFire, MEGA, Google Drive, etc.) instead of GitHub Releases, so the file can't be reviewed.

contentRules.title: Hidden encoded payload in web page
contentRules.description: An HTML page hides a large encoded blob in an invisible element - used by fake download pages to deliver malware.

contentRules.title: Download link/button leads off-GitHub
contentRules.description: README has a prominent "Download" link or button image that points to an external site instead of GitHub Releases - common in fake-software repos.

contentRules.title: README pushes a packaged archive download
contentRules.description: Links straight to a .rar/.zip/.7z in Releases. Legit projects do this too, but combined with a lure topic or no source code it is the classic fake-software pattern.

contentRules.title: Scheduled workflow that keeps committing
contentRules.description: A workflow runs on a frequent schedule and pushes commits - often used to fake activity so a malicious repo looks maintained and ranks higher in search.

pathRules.title: Disguised executable (double extension)
pathRules.description: A file pretending to be a document/image but actually executable.

pathRules.title: Shortcut / HTA / script-host file
pathRules.description: File types (.lnk, .hta, .vbe, .wsf, .scf, .cpl) rarely used legitimately in source repos.

pathRules.title: Executable committed to repo
pathRules.description: Windows executables/DLLs checked into source code can't be reviewed and may be malware.

pathRules.title: Archive committed to repo
pathRules.description: Zip/rar/7z files in the source tree can hide content from review.

pathRules.title: Release ships Windows executables
pathRules.description: Releases contain .exe/.msi/.scr files. Normal for apps - but verify the project is reputable.

pathRules.title: Randomly named workflow file
pathRules.description: Workflow file names like 'miipAmXWgVIR.yml' are generated by malware campaigns that mass-produce fake repos.

pathRules.title: Release ships a .rar/.7z archive
pathRules.description: Password-protected RAR/7z archives are the usual way malware dodges GitHub's scanning.
